newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Metals weigh on Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Metals weigh on Australian stocks at open.

text.p: The Australian share market dipped at the open on Tuesday as miners again felt the weight of weaker base metals prices in offshore markets.
At the opening, the All Ordinaries index fell 7.3 points to 2,260.5. September share price index futures slipped four points to 2,268, a 7.5 point premium to the underlying index.
Record breaking runs by the bulls on Wall Street failed to impress local investors, most of whom put their attention squarely on the major miners as base metals prices continued to sag.
"Miners are the leaders again," said a Sydney broker, adding that he saw little optimism for metal prices in the near term.
"Metals (prices) are not showing any signs of improvement at the moment," he said.

Underlining the source of the bourse's weakness, the All Resources index slipped 0.6 percent in early trade, compared to an All Industrials index dip of just 0.11 percent and a fall in the benchmark All Ordinaries index of 0.3 percent.
BHP and WMC suffered most. BHP announced a big jump in copper output from its 57.5 percent owned Escondida mine in Chile.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to six, while about 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
